issues.body:
The anchor read is `... || true`, so `last` ends up empty in three distinct situations: (1) every one of the newest 30 runs concluded `action_required`, (2) the workflow has no runs at all (never fired, or its runs aged out of retention), and (3) the `gh api` call itself failed — a 5xx, a rate limit, a network blip — which `|| true` swallows silently. The new annotation asserts case (1) unconditionally: "has no accepted run among its newest 30; action_required runs are not liveness evidence".

Control flow is correct in all three cases (prev=0 -> stale -> kick, which is the intended fail-open), so this is a diagnostics defect, not a behaviour defect. But this repo has an explicit, hard-won norm against exactly this conflation: ci-latency-alert.py's M4 census keeps `not-sampled` and `rejected-jobs-unreadable` as SEPARATE states precisely because "a workflow that DOES carry a cron but whose runs were never listed is INSIDE the population and UNREAD, which is not the same as healthy". The comment in this diff names that alarm as the owner of human recovery — so an annotation that misattributes an API outage to ingestion rejection points the human at the wrong M4 finding.

Same text at .github/workflows/dashboard.yml:520 and :580, and .github/workflows/metrics.yml:305.
issues.fix_hint: Capture the read's own success separately from its emptiness, e.g. drop `|| true` into an explicit `if ! last=$(gh api ...); then last=""; read_ok=0; fi`, and emit one of three distinct messages: a read failure, a listing with zero runs, and a listing whose newest 30 are all `action_required`. Only the third should claim rejection. If that is too much shell for this leg, at minimum soften the wording to state the observation rather than the cause ("no accepted run was READ for ${wf} — the listing was empty, unreadable, or entirely action_required").
issues.title: Empty `last` conflates an UNREAD run listing with an observed rejected stream, so the new ::error:: can state a cause it never established

issues.body:
The stated invariant in the rewritten comment is that the run anchor is valid only where "an accepted run IMPLIES the workflow did its work". `action_required` is now excluded, but `startup_failure` — GitHub's conclusion for a run it created and could not start — satisfies the same counterexample exactly, and is left in. A workflow stuck emitting `startup_failure` on every cron fire would still read as permanently live to all three legs: the #922/#1375 blindness recurring in one conclusion over.

This repo already codifies the concept: scripts/dispatch-claim.py:547 defines `BROKEN_CONCLUSIONS = {"cancelled", "action_required", "startup_failure", "stale", ...}` for precisely "a run that produced nothing". I am flagging this as minor rather than major because #1375's MEASURED fingerprint is `action_required` + jobs=0 (dashboard-gen.py:4968, PR #1363/#1364), so the diff does fix the defect it was scoped to — but the gap is one line wide and the same class of outage.

Note `cancelled` deserves separate thought before being added: singleton concurrency groups cancel superseded runs routinely, and there the surviving run DID work, so blanket-excluding `cancelled` could over-kick.
issues.fix_hint: Widen the select to the conclusions that mean "created but executed nothing", e.g. `select((.conclusion // "") | IN("action_required", "startup_failure") | not)`, and add one dashboard-gen.py row per added conclusion mirroring the `[#1375] a fresh action_required run cannot hide ...` pair so the widening is not vacuous. Update the `::error::` wording to name the set rather than only `action_required`. If `startup_failure` is deliberately out of scope for this PR, say so in the comment beside the filter and reference the issue that carries it — an undocumented omission here reads as an oversight next time this leg is audited.
issues.title: Only `action_required` is excluded; `startup_failure` (and the rest of this repo's own BROKEN_CONCLUSIONS set) still count as liveness

issues.body:
_PUBLISH_KICK_GH_STUB is rewritten to serve the two per_page=30 shapes, and its anchor branch hardcodes `"conclusion":"success"`. That keeps the three existing `_run_publish_kick` rows (scripts/metrics.py:2376-2388) green, but no row in this file ever supplies an `action_required` run, so metrics.yml's OWN suite never asserts the behaviour the PR exists to add. The coverage lives entirely in scripts/dashboard-gen.py, which drives metrics.yml's leg as the mesh's third source.

This is not vacuous — I checked the reversion path: deleting the `select(.conclusion != "action_required")` from metrics.yml makes the argv miss both stub patterns, hit `*) exit 64`, and (via `|| true`) empty the anchor, so the `last_run_age=60` row at :2381 sees an unexpected dispatch and reds. So the mutation is killed, just indirectly and with a confusing failure message. The concern is locality: a reader of metrics.py sees a stub that models `action_required` routing and no row that exercises it.
issues.fix_hint: Add a `rejected_run=True`-style parameter to `_run_publish_kick` (or a STUB_LAST_RUN_CONCLUSION env) and two rows in this file mirroring dashboard-gen.py's pair: a fresh `action_required` run ahead of a stale accepted one still kicks, and a pure rejected stream kicks AND emits the `::error::`. Alternatively, add a one-line comment above _PUBLISH_KICK_GH_STUB pointing at the dashboard-gen.py rows that own this leg's #1375 coverage, so the stub's `action_required` branch is not orphaned.
issues.title: metrics.py's stub is reshaped to keep passing but its own suite gains no #1375 assertion

issues.body: The THE ANCHOR block was rewrapped to insert the #1375 paragraph, and the edit ends a line at "since the #819 tick" with roughly half the column budget unused, continuing "# floor, a within-floor ring concludes ..." on the next. It reads correctly but scans as an accidental leftover from the hunk rather than deliberate wrapping, in a comment block whose density is otherwise carefully maintained.
issues.fix_hint: Re-flow the paragraph so "#819 tick floor" sits on one line, matching the surrounding wrap width.
issues.title: Comment rewrap leaves `# #819 tick` / `# floor,` split mid-phrase with most of the line unused

verdict.summary:
#1375: the run-anchored keepalive legs stop treating GitHub's ingestion-rejected runs (conclusion `action_required`, jobs=0 — the fingerprint ci-latency-alert.py's M4 already documents at scripts/ci-latency-alert.py:282-315) as liveness evidence. All THREE production readers are updated consistently — dashboard.yml's registry leg (:513), its cross-repo sparq leg (:576), and metrics.yml's third mesh leg (:301) — swapping `.workflow_runs[0].created_at` over `per_page=1` for `[... | select(.conclusion != "action_required") | .created_at] | max // empty` over `per_page=30`. Semantics check out: `max` over ISO-8601 Z stamps is lexicographically the newest accepted run; `[] | max` is null and `null // empty` yields the empty string, so a fully-rejected stream falls through to prev=0 and kicks, preserving the leg's documented fail-open. In-progress runs carry `conclusion: null`, which passes the filter, so the #559 fail-open path (unreadable live check -> consult age) behaves exactly as before. The per_page=30 window is not a truncation risk: every watched cadence (900-3600s) puts far fewer than 30 runs inside its threshold. dispatch.yml's marker anchor is untouched, as is ingestion-alarm.yml's newest-run read (correctly, it is the detector, not a liveness proxy).

Test validity: the new rows are NOT vacuous. I traced the kill for the obvious mutation — drop the `select(...)` and the anchor becomes max over all runs, i.e. the 60s-old rejected stamp, so "[#1375] a fresh action_required run cannot hide the newest accepted run's stale age" flips from kicked=[metrics.yml] to kicked=[] and reds. The pure-rejected rows additionally pin the literal `::error::` text, and the same pair is driven through all three real leg bodies. The `code = 64 if "gh-stub: unexpected argv:" in log` promotion in run_keepalive_leg is a genuine hardening: production's `|| true` would otherwise let a stub refusal masquerade as an empty stale anchor and satisfy the outcome rows. … [truncated 495 chars]
